transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well… I came in because of what’s been going on with my husband’s sister. She’s been working this family business, you know, getting herself in the middle of everything, and I can see she’s trying to get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep saying, “Oh, that’s not what’s happening,” trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been going on more than a year now.

And I don’t like coming to places like this, to be honest. I almost didn’t, because last time I had to fill out a bunch of papers and they kept asking about my schooling, and that just… anyway. I’m here because nobody’s taking it seriously.
Are you absolutely certain that your husband’s sister is trying to take control of the money and push you out?

Yes, I’m certain. I mean, people act like I’m making a mountain out of it, but I’ve been watching this for over a year. She keeps getting herself into the family business, into the money side, and then suddenly I’m not included in decisions the way I should be. And, you know, my husband says I’m reading into things, but he doesn’t notice details like I do—he’ll misplace the light bill and then say nobody told him it came, so… but yes, I know what I’ve been seeing.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I hear people talking when they’re actually there, or the TV if it’s on, things like that. Sometimes the house makes noises and I’ll think, “What was that?” but voices when nobody’s there… no, not really.
Have you had any major medical illness or injury to your brain?

I don’t think so… I mean, nothing like, you know, some big brain injury that I know of. I’ve had the usual things happen over the years, bumps here and there, headaches sometimes, but who doesn’t? My husband acts like every little thing is a crisis unless it’s something I’m pointing out, then suddenly it’s “not a big deal.” But no, I haven’t been told I had some major brain problem or anything like that.
Aside from your husband’s sister, do you believe anyone else is deliberately trying to harm you or plot against you?

No, not really anyone else like that. It’s mainly her—my husband’s sister. That’s why I came in, because she’s been working her way into the family business and the money side of things, and then somehow I’m the one left out of decisions. People keep trying to make it sound harmless, like family just “helping out,” but I’ve been seeing it for more than a year. 

I mean, other people go along with things sometimes because they don’t want trouble, you know how families are—everybody smiles at holidays and then talks in the kitchen—but the one pushing it, the one trying to get control and push me out, is her.
Has anyone shown you clear proof that your husband’s sister is not trying to take control of the money and push you out?

No. They say things, sure—like “that’s not what’s happening” or “you’re reading into it”—but that’s not proof. That’s just smoothing things over because nobody wants to admit what she’s doing.

I came here because my husband’s sister has been working her way into the family business and the money decisions, and then I’m the one getting pushed out. And it’s been going on for more than a year now. You start noticing little things, who gets called, who doesn’t, who knows about something before you do… I mean, people can dress it up however they want, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Before all this with your husband’s sister started, did you generally tend to mistrust other people’s motives?

I don’t know… I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful with people, because you never really know what someone is thinking. But I wouldn’t say I walked around mistrusting everybody or anything like that.

Like, I used to help neighbors with little things, and I’d talk to people at family gatherings—well, depending on who was there, because some people just stir things up. But this thing with my husband’s sister is different. It’s not just me being suspicious for no reason. It’s what started happening, the way things changed.
Has anyone told you that your speech has become hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?

I don’t think so… not that anyone’s said it to me like that. Sometimes people act like they don’t want to listen, but that’s different, you know? Like if you’re trying to explain something and they already made up their mind, then of course they say you’re “going on” or whatever.

But no, I haven’t really been told my thoughts are jumbled. I mean, I know what I’m trying to say. Sometimes it takes a minute because there’s a lot connected to it.
If you were shown clear records proving your husband’s sister was not taking control of the money, would you accept that?

If they were real clear records, I’d look at them, sure. But papers can be shown one way and still not show what’s really happening, you know? People leave things out, or they only show the part that makes it look harmless.

Because I came here about this for a reason. My husband’s sister has been getting herself into the family business and the money decisions, and then somehow I’m the one not included. And this has been going on for over a year, not just one little misunderstanding. Folks keep trying to smooth it over, but I know what I’ve been seeing.
Before this situation with your husband’s sister, did people in your life often tell you that you were too suspicious or had trouble trusting others?

I don’t really remember people saying it that way, like “you’re too suspicious.” Maybe sometimes somebody would say I worry too much, but people say that when they don’t want to talk about something.

Before all this, I was mostly just going about my business, you know—keeping the house together, dealing with family things. I’ve always felt you have to be careful who you trust, but that’s just common sense to me. My mother used to say not everybody smiling at you is for you, and I think about that sometimes. But no, I can’t say people were always telling me I had some big problem trusting people.
Have you ever felt that someone was putting thoughts into your mind?

Putting thoughts into my mind? I don’t know… I don’t think of it like that. My thoughts feel like mine, even if sometimes I’m trying to sort out where everything fits.

I mean, people can influence you, sure. Like family gets in your ear, says things a certain way, and then you’re left thinking about it all night while you’re trying to make dinner or remember if you paid the light bill. But that’s not the same as somebody putting a thought in there, I don’t think. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
During this past year, have you had a period where your mood was unusually high or irritable for days at a time?

I’m not sure what you mean by unusually high. I mean, I’ve had days where I’m worked up or aggravated, especially with all this family business going on, but I wouldn’t say I was, like, feeling on top of the world for days or anything.

I do get irritated—anybody would, if they felt pushed aside. But it’s not like some separate spell that came over me, if that’s what you mean. Some days are just heavier than others, and then you still have to make dinner, answer the phone, do what needs doing.
Before this started with your husband’s sister, did you generally trust people?

Generally? I guess… I trusted people enough. I mean, you have to trust some folks, right? You can’t go through life thinking everybody’s up to something. But I was never the type to just tell everybody my business either.

Like with neighbors, I’d be polite, wave, maybe talk about the weather or whose trash can blew over, but that doesn’t mean I’m inviting them into everything. My aunt used to say keep your front room clean and your private things private, and I think that’s just how I was raised.

So… I don’t know if I’d say I trusted people completely. I was careful. But I don’t remember it being some big issue before all this.
Have you been keeping notes, records, or other proof about what your husband’s sister is doing?

I mean, I’ve tried to keep things straight, because after a while people act like you’re just misunderstanding. I don’t have it all in some fancy file or anything, but I know what I’ve been seeing.

That’s really why I came here. My husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. And folks try to smooth it over, say “oh, that’s just how she is,” or “don’t worry about it,” but it’s been going on more than a year now. You don’t just imagine that kind of thing over and over.
Do you often feel that harmless comments or actions from other people are actually meant as insults or attacks on you?

I don’t go around thinking every little thing is about me, no. Like, if somebody says the soup is salty, I’m not sitting there crying that they called me a bad cook.

But with his sister… that’s different. People make these little comments and then act innocent, and later it turns into her getting more say in the family business, more control over the money, and me being pushed out like I don’t matter. Folks try to smooth it over, say I’m taking it wrong, but I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s been going on too long for it to be nothing.
Do you believe your husband’s sister is definitely trying to push you out and take control of the money?

Yes… I do. I mean, I don’t know how else to say it. She’s been working things around in that family business so she can have more control over the money, and so I’m left out of decisions.

And people keep trying to make it sound nicer than it is, like, “Oh, she’s just helping,” or “Don’t take it that way.” But after more than a year of watching it happen, you start to know what you’re seeing. It’s not just one little thing. It’s the pattern.
Has anyone in your close family ever had schizophrenia or another psychotic illness?

I don’t really know of anyone like that in my close family. I mean, people in families have their moods, and my mother’s side had plenty of arguing, but nobody ever sat down and said, “this person has that illness,” not to me anyway.

And you know how families are, they don’t always tell you the truth about things. They’ll hide money problems, drinking, all kinds of things, so who knows what got covered up. But as far as I know, no, not schizophrenia or something like that.
Have there been times when you felt confused or not fully clear-headed?

Confused? I don’t know… not really like that, I don’t think. I mean, sometimes I get tired and my head feels full, especially when everybody’s talking over each other or acting like I’m the one making trouble.

But not confused like I don’t know where I am or anything. Sometimes people say I’m “not thinking clearly” just because I don’t agree with them, and that’s different. My husband does that sometimes, he’ll say, “Calm down, you’re not seeing it right,” but that doesn’t mean I’m confused. It just means they don’t want to hear what I’m saying.
Aside from this issue with your husband’s sister, have you had any other strong beliefs that other people said were not true?

No, I mean… not really other things like that. This is the thing I came about. It’s my husband’s sister and the family business, and the way she’s been working it so she gets more control over the money and I get pushed out of decisions.

People keep trying to smooth it over, you know, make it sound like I’m taking it wrong, but I’ve been watching it for more than a year. You see enough little things add up, you know what you’re seeing.
Have you usually been very sensitive to criticism from other people?

I don’t know… I mean, nobody likes being criticized, right? If someone says something fair, I can hear it, but a lot of times people call it “criticism” when they’re really just taking a dig.

Like my aunt used to do that at dinners, she’d say, “Oh, you’re wearing that?” and then act like she was helping. That kind of thing sticks with you. But sensitive… I don’t know if I’d use that word. Depends who’s saying it and how they say it.

And people keep trying to make it sound nicer than it is, like, “Oh, she’s just helping,” or “Don’t take it that way.” But after more than a year of watching it happen, you start to know what you’re seeing. It’s not just one little thing. It’s the pattern.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a first-degree family history of psychotic disorders, which would help distinguish a primary delusional disorder from a psychotic disorder due to another medical condition.
doctor.question: Has anyone in your close family ever had schizophrenia or another psychotic illness?

target_item.reason: The question asks about family history of schizophrenia or another psychotic illness, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t really know of anyone like that in my close family. I mean, people in families have their moods, and my mother’s side had plenty of arguing, but nobody ever sat down and said, “this person has that illness,” not to me anyway.

And you know how families are, they don’t always tell you the truth about things. They’ll hide money problems, drinking, all kinds of things, so who knows what got covered up. But as far as I know, no, not schizophrenia or something like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been any clouding of consciousness or confusion suggestive of an organic psychotic disorder rather than delusional disorder or paranoid personality traits.
doctor.question: Have there been times when you felt confused or not fully clear-headed?

target_item.reason: The question asks about confusion or not being fully clear-headed, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
Confused? I don’t know… not really like that, I don’t think. I mean, sometimes I get tired and my head feels full, especially when everybody’s talking over each other or acting like I’m the one making trouble.

But not confused like I don’t know where I am or anything. Sometimes people say I’m “not thinking clearly” just because I don’t agree with them, and that’s different. My husband does that sometimes, he’ll say, “Calm down, you’re not seeing it right,” but that doesn’t mean I’m confused. It just means they don’t want to hear what I’m saying.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a fixed delusional disorder from schizotypal/paranoid personality by testing whether the suspicious belief is isolated to this one theme rather than part of a broader lifelong pattern of odd beliefs or ideas of reference.
doctor.question: Aside from this issue with your husband’s sister, have you had any other strong beliefs that other people said were not true?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions, and no matter how folks try to smooth it over, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the presence of other fixed, strongly held beliefs that others dispute, which directly concerns delusions.

patient.answer:
No, I mean… not really other things like that. This is the thing I came about. It’s my husband’s sister and the family business, and the way she’s been working it so she gets more control over the money and I get pushed out of decisions.

People keep trying to smooth it over, you know, make it sound like I’m taking it wrong, but I’ve been watching it for more than a year. You see enough little things add up, you know what you’re seeing.

inference.note: Single persistent non-bizarre persecutory belief >1 year, no hallucinations, thought disorder, mood episode, confusion, or medical/organic features; this rules against F23.3 and F06.2. Paranoid personality traits remain a differential but appear not pervasive premorbidly, making F22 most likely.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a longstanding pattern of hypersensitivity to criticism, which would support paranoid personality disorder over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you usually been very sensitive to criticism from other people?

target_item.reason: The question asks about sensitivity to criticism, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… I mean, nobody likes being criticized, right? If someone says something fair, I can hear it, but a lot of times people call it “criticism” when they’re really just taking a dig.

Like my aunt used to do that at dinners, she’d say, “Oh, you’re wearing that?” and then act like she was helping. That kind of thing sticks with you. But sensitive… I don’t know if I’d use that word. Depends who’s saying it and how they say it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a single fixed persecutory belief focused on her husband's sister taking control of family business finances and excluding her, persisting for over a year. She repeatedly expresses strong conviction despite others disagreeing, while denying hallucinations, thought insertion, disorganized thinking, confusion, manic episodes, major brain illness, and broader psychotic symptoms. The suspiciousness appears circumscribed rather than a longstanding pervasive personality pattern, making persistent delusional disorder more likely than paranoid personality disorder.
